how: Declared from a profile of every record of each type (operating.pg.date_declare profile): a field is a date only when its filled cells read as calendar days (dated/filled >= 0.99); the date of record is the first such field, in the curator's order of business dates, whose cells cover at least half of the type's records (else the best-covered). The meaning of a Sage column is from the Sage 300 data dictionary and is backed here by measured evidence: coverage, range, future share, and for a later date the share of rows on or after the date of record. role: record = the date of record; stamp = the system's own last-write stamp (operating.pg.date_declare.STAMP_FIELDS), declared the date of record only when no business date is filled in at least 90% of the records; other = another date the row carries.

Customer required date (a planned date). When no FM or gold date is held and the date comes from Sage, it is Sage's expected ship date (oe_order_header.expdate), the date the order is promised to leave, not a date the customer asked for; the citation names the field.

Business Central's lastModifiedDateTime: BC sets it on every write of the record (a source change signal).

The Portal row's updated_at: naive UTC wall time as Prisma writes it, kept as text (it states no zone). The Portal's ETL and bridges bump it whether or not a field changed: a stamp, never proof of a change.
